references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

certifications_partner.text: o facilitate this, the Department provides an in-house “Fixture Script” library which provides a pattern. Fixture scripts can also be used within the running application, facilitating manual/exploratory testing (discussed below). The Department also provides a number of other libraries to manage fixtures. The simple “fake data” library can be used in unit and other tests to select/generate a random value for use within a test. Integration tests should not hard-code any officer user Ids, instead the “officer leasing” library allows an unused user/officer account to be exclusively used, with logic to automatically check/reset the officer’s certificates for signed recorded actions. Production code should never use system time directly, instead it should be possible to “mock the clock” in tests. For the BOMi application the “Programmable Clock” service provides this capability. Keeping Tests Green Whenever a project starts the Department will ensure that the initial CI pipeline for their project branch (of the Trunk) is green. Thereafter it is the responsibility of the project to keep the pipeline “green”. The Department uses a number of approaches to achieve this. B2B: The DSP API and Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI) APIs enable business-to-business integration to other Departments, public service bodies and to other European countries. Other supporting systems that make up the technology landscape include Facial Imaging Matching System (FIMS), and the General Registers Office (GRO) system. The BOMi’s scope will continue to grow in both size and complexity to (a) support the Department’s expanding Digital requirements, (b) consolidate its technology stack, and (c) continue to support new or changing legislation as it arises. The current technology platform is .NET Framework 4.x deployed to Windows Servers. In due course these will be upgraded to .NET 6 (aka .NET Core) at which time the Department will plan to deploy these systems, either for testing and/or production, on Linux/Docker when appropriate. New systems also target .NET 6 for the same purpose. The Department’s development resources are a combination of the Department’s internal staff, partnering with a number of service providers. The Senior Technical Development Advisor (TDA Lot 1) has acted as an independent strategic technical advisor across the IS Division, providing guidance on a range of SDLC and architecture related concerns. The TDA (Lot 1) helped product and platform teams deliver secure, resilient, and high-quality solutions more rapidly through the adoption of modern engineering practices and automation technologies. The TDA (Lot 1) role focused on shaping governance process and technical direction and procurement activities, translating complex technical issues into clear recommendations and implementation plans. Key areas of contribution included Continuous Integration, Release and Deployment, SDLC platform engineering, application security process and governance, Test Data Management modernisation, Developer Experience, contract testing, and SDLC platform architecture, particularly for the Department’s BOMi Platform. The TDA (Lot 1) also played a significant role in defining product and platform ownership models, associated team charters and enhanced IT governance approaches. In addition, the role supported various technical procurements through technical assessments.

ESB was established in 1927 as a statutory corporation in the Republic of Ireland under the Electricity (Supply) Act 1927. With a holding of approximately 97.1%, ESB is majority owned by the Irish Government. The remaining approximate 2.9% is held by the trustees of an Employee Share Ownership Plan. As a strong, diversified, vertically integrated utility, ESB operates right across the electricity market: from generation, through transmission and distribution, to supply. In addition, ESB extracts further value at certain points along this chain: supplying gas, using our networks to carry fibre for telecommunications, developing electric vehicle public charging infrastructure and more. ESB is a leading Irish utility focused on providing excellent customer service and maintaining our financial strength. We have a regulated asset base of approximately €12 billion with 30% of electricity generation capacity in the all-island market.

It also provides historical data that is very important for recognising trends and proactively addressing issues. Lepinguga ja lepingulisaga võetud kohustuste täitmiseks edastatakse arendajale või riigihanke pakkumusest tulenevale allvolitatud töötlejale andmed sh isikuandmed ja eriliiki isikuandmed krüpteeritult või tagatakse turvatud serveril asuvale piiratud ligipääsuga failile ligipääs krüpteeritud püsiühenduse kaudu ning lepingu objekti rakenduse administraator il on õigu s saata vajadusel isikuandmed sh eriliiki isikuandmeid saabunud taotluse alusel andmesubjektile krüpteeritult. 3.3.4. Lepinguga ja lepingulisaga võetud kohustuste täitmiseks loodava rakenduse logisid säilitatakse vastavalt vastutava töötleja andmeturbepoliitikale ja ISO 27001 standardile ning andme -, süsteemi- ja arenduse töötlusega seotud logisid säilitatakse kuni kaks kuud tekkimisest. Lepingu objekti rakenduses kasutatakse Microsoft 365 keskkond a, mis säilitab logisid vastavalt Microsofti teenustingimustele ja üldmäärusele, EL majanduspiirkonnas. V olitatud töötleja kui v astutav arenduse teostaja sh volitatud koordineeriv arendaja säilitab turvakoopiaid kuni andmete kustutamiseni 2 (kaks) aastat. 3.3.5. Lepinguga ja lepingulisaga võetud kohustuste täitmiseks ning lepingu objekti a ndmete juhuslikku hävimise ja kahjustamise vastu peab volitatud töötleja kui vastutav arenduse teostaja ja volitatud

tavalt Microsofti teenustingimustele ja üldmäärusele, EL majanduspiirkonnas. Lepinguga ja lepingulisaga võetud kohustuste täitmiseks ning lepingu objekti a ndmete juhuslikku hävimise ja kahjustamise vastu peab volitatud töötleja kui vastutav arenduse teostaja ja volitatud koordineeriv arendaja rakendama tehnilisi ja korralduslikke meetmeid sh säilitama kõiki arendusega seotud andmeid turvatud serveris sh Riigi IT Keskuse (RIT) halduses olevas serveris, mis vastab EITS või ISO 27001 standardile ja üldmääruse nõuetele ning tegema regulaarseid varukoopiaid, rakendama krüpteerimist ja ligipääsupiiranguid isikuandmete ja eriliiki isikuandmete töötlemisel. Andmete kogumise perioodi faasis kasutatakse Zone keskkonda kasutajate nimede ja muude andmete sisestamiseks , kuid anonüümset andmestikku säilitatakse krüpteeritud Microsoft 365 keskkonnas (SharePoint/OneDrive, EL majanduspiirkonnas). 3.4. Kui pakkumuse esitavad mitu pakkujat ühiselt (ühispakkujad), tuleb hankepass esitada iga ühispakkumuse esitamisel osaleva ettevõtja kohta. 4. Pakkumuse vastavustingimused ja kontroll 4.1. Pakkumuse vastavustingimused on esitatud RHR-i rubriigis „Vastavustingimused“. 4.2. Hankija kontrollib esitatud pakkumuse vastavust RHAD-s esitatud tingimustele ning teeb põhjendatud kirjaliku otsuse pakkumuste vastavaks tunnistamise või pakkumuste tagasi lükkamise kohta. 4.3. Meeskonnaliikmete nõuetele vastavust kontrollib hankija pakkuja poolt Lisa 4 vormidel (isikute CV-d) esitatud andmete alusel. Täiendavalt võib hankija kontrollida esitatud andmeid hankijale avalikes andmekogudes kättesaadava info kaudu. Hankijal on õigus lisateabe saamiseks pöörduda kolmandate isikute poole. Hankijal on õigus pakkujalt küsida täiendavat lisainfot ja dokumente, mis kinnitavad pakkumuses esitatud andmete õigsust. Pakkuja peab esitama hankija nõutud andmed/dokumendid 3 (kolme) tööpäeva jooksul. Nõutud vormide mittenõuetekohasel täitmisel ja/või hankija poolt küsitud täiendava info või dokumentide esitamata jätmisel on hankijal õigus tunnistada pakkumus mittevastavaks. 4.4.
